steps.text: In a medium soup pot melt butter over low heat, and saute onions until tender. Stir in the mashed potatoes, and then slowly add the chicken broth. Stirring, add milk (use more or less to achieve desired creaminess). Cook until heated through and season with salt and pepper to taste.

raw_recipe.headline: Potato Soup
raw_recipe.description: A great way to use leftover mashed potatoes! Milk and chicken broth complete the soup. Also can be made with fresh potatoes, and leeks instead of onions . Garnish with chives for an extra touch.
raw_recipe.name: Potato Soup

recipeInstructions.text: In a medium soup pot melt butter over low heat, and saute onions until tender. Stir in the mashed potatoes, and then slowly add the chicken broth. Stirring, add milk (use more or less to achieve desired creaminess). Cook until heated through and season with salt and pepper to taste.

review.reviewBody: This is a great starter recipe. I put a little garlic in with the onions, then add diced raw potato, leaving some chunks larger than others. Then put the potato in the sauce pan with the onion, salt and pepper them and let it fry a little so the potatoes get a nice flavor going. Then I add chicken broth and bring to a boil til the potatoes soften.Lastly the milk or cream whichever I have on hand. I always add bacon crumbles and garnish with shredded cheddar and a glop of sour cream. The only reason I don't give this recipe 5 stars is I think it needs another seasoning but I haven't quite figured out what yet. My picky husband asks me to make this all the time, though.

I used this recipe for inspiration, but I modified it. I sauteed 2 tbsp butter, 1 diced onion, and 3 minced cloves of garlic. I then added 2 tbsp flour and coated the aromatics, stirring while sauteeing. I added a carton of chicken stock and a bay leaf and brought it to a boil. Then, I added the mashed potatoes (I only had about 3 cups). I brought that to a boil, then blended with an immersion blender. I added a half cup of heavy cream, pepper, and salt, to taste. As I made it with my improvisations, I thought it was very tasty. I will be making this again.

I did make changes but essentially it was the same. I had not made mashed potatoes right before seeing this recipe but went for it anyway! So I boiled my potatoes, and then seeing all the starch being released didn't want that to go to waste so I put away the chicken broth and instead poured the water into a measuring cup, added chicken base, mixed, then added the broth back to the saucepan. I then used an immersion blender on the potato and liquid, added the onion (and the garlic I'd cooked with the onion). I then blended it a bit more before adding the milk (and some cream), and topped it off with some bacon (which I DID have cooked in the fridge) as I served it. We don't peel the potatoes when we make mashed potatoes so I'd didn't here either. That helped it all remain quite quick and the soup tasted good!

Great base recipe! To add flavor I used about 1/4 cup of butter to fry the onion in, added a cube of chicken bouillon, a couple TBSP of dried chives, and replaced the milk with sour cream. Also cubed a can of potatoes for potato chunks. Topped with shredded cheddar, bacon bits and green onions for a loaded version. It was amazing. Thanks for the recipe!

I am from New Mexico, and the missing spice is HATCH GREEN CHILIES! Just a small can , (about 2 oz.) makes all the flavors in this potato soup come alive!!! Other than that, it is nearly the perfect potato soup! I have to add, that I also fry the bigger chunks of potato with the butter & onion, and I also add roasted garlic, crumbled bacon, a tablespoon of creamy horseradish, and some shredded cheese to top it off. That, just in my Southwestern opinion, is something that DOES make this a 5 star recipe!

I peeled and sliced russet potatoes. Cooked in instant pot until soft enough to mash. Proceeded with recipe adjusting amounts to go with the quantity of potatoes I had. I cooked bacon until crisp and chopped it up. Added the bacon bits to the soup and topped my bowl with shredded sharp cheddar cheese. I used garlic powder and pepper for seasoning. Will make again.

I made this and it was very good. My boyfriend liked it, and that says a lot. I used everyone's suggestions, started with ready made mashed potatoes, added 1 regular can of chicken broth, chopped 1 large onion and cooked it with 1 tbsp garlic in butter, added 6 cubed potatoes that were boiled 8 min. I also added cubed ham. I mixed it together then added half and half and 1/2 tsp dried basil,1/2 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp dried parsley. I simmered it a few min. And served it up with shredded cheese and sour cream. Easy to make, and so very good.

I made this soup tonight and it's good although next time I'll cut down on the broth so the soup is thicker (personal preference) since there is not much seasoning I'd suggest making sure your mashed potatoes are well seasoned...I cooked the onion with my potatoes and added minced garlic..to my mashed potatoes I add butter, garlic salt and cream cheese which makes for a very tasty soup I'll definitely make this again

I added about a pound of bacon . Then used some of the grease in place of the butter since the potatoes had butter in them already. I added a diced red bell pepper and 2 cloves minced garlic to the onions. Then cut the broth down 1/3 cup and stirred sour cream in at the end. I also added some grated sharp cheddar.

i fried chopped bacon with the onion and minced garlic.... also i boiled chopped celery in the chicken broth... before mashing the potatoes i scooped some out and added them to the broth and bacon... then when the potatoes were mashed i mixed it all together... added the milk, some salt and peper, and a tad bit of Italian... 


soooooo delicious...

I do love that this recipe doesn't have flour, which can really steal a soup's flavor. As has been said, this soup is only bland if your mashed potatoes are bland. 
Doubling the recipe, I made my potatoes with generous garlic, 3 cups shredded cheddar cheese, a tub of cottage cheese, 18 strips of bacon, 7 cups of corn, and 3 onions sauteed in leftover bacon fat. (Cooking the onions in bacon fat really gave the whole soup an AMAZING bacon flavor. It was devoured.)
I also HALVED the amount of chicken broth in the soup, and compensated with some milk. 
I do imagine the recipe as-is would be bland, hence 3 stars. But it's a great base to work from if improv is your thing!
This recipe was simple to follow and has a traditional potato soup flavor. With the addition of a sprinkle of cheese or bacon it would truly be amazing.
I would add chicken meat.

NOT the most delicious soup ever; it was the most BOR-ing soup ever. I did NOT alter the recipe in any way, just to make sure I could rate it correctly (I knew it would be bland.) A child could slap this together. Send some great recipes, not all beginner.

Like many others, I thought this was kind of blah so I supplemented with garlic, frozen corn, and bacon, then sprinkled with cheddar. Turned out yummy. Had to make a batch of mashed potatoes. Who has SIX CUPS of leftover mashed potatoes???

Used 2 packages of Idahoan mashed potatoes I made with a little beer along with water in the package instructions. Used cream instead of milk for soup. Garnished with packaged fried onions from the produce department, chives and bacon as called for. Pretzel crackers and BOY-OH-BOY!
it was okay. I pureed the onions and added a minced clove of garlic just give a little kick
Delicious, fast and easy. I started by making instant mashed potatoes adding the onions to the liquid before adding potato flakes. Added some shredded cheddar and hormel bacon bits. So good!

Hi. I like how my soup turned out. I amended it and the final soup that I made turned out well and has a good flavor. Thank you for the recipe that I used and then changed to fit the ingredients that I had etc. Nowelle
My family loved it- so quick and easy. I added fresh cheddar cheese, some garlic, corn and bacon bits. Served with sour dough bread and a light salad.
